title: Study on Profile of Individuals Providing Informal and Unpaid Caregiving
what_it_is: Study on Profile of Individuals Providing Informal and Unpaid Caregiving

sections.label: Caregiver age groups and data gaps
sections.summary: It gives numbers of residents by age group and states there is no specific data on unpaid caregivers or those without means.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Of these, around 3,000 were aged 15 to 29; 17,000 were aged 30 to 39; 22,000 were aged 40 to 49; and 47,000 were aged 50 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: We do not have specific data on the number of residents who are carrying out unpaid caregiving and how many do not have the means to support themselves when they become seniors.

sections.label: No caregiving productivity study
sections.summary: It states no study has been done on caregiving's impact on productivity and employment, but employment and unemployment rates are monitored.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: On whether there has been a study on the impact on productivity and the employment rate for adults as a result of growing caregiving demand, we have not taken on such a study yet, but we have been monitoring very closely the employment rate as well as unemployment rate for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Employers providing caregiving leave
sections.summary: It states that in 2022 about 58% of employers voluntarily provided additional paid caregiving leave and over 4,000 adopted a tripartite standard.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In 2022, about 58% of employers voluntarily provided additional paid caregiving leave, such as family care leave for their employees, and more than 4,000 employers have also adopted the tripartite standard on unpaid leave for unexpected care needs.

sections.label: Enhanced Home Caregiving Grant
sections.summary: It states MOH enhanced the Home Caregiving Grant to give financial support to families in certain household income categories.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) has also enhanced the Home Caregiving Grant, in recognition that some financial support would be helpful for families of certain household income categories.

sections.label: Career support for caregivers
sections.summary: It states there are career conversion programmes, upskilling resources, career trials and other career support measures for caregivers returning to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: First, on the support for caregivers who might want to return to work, there are career conversion programmes, upskilling resources, career trials and a whole string of career support measures that are available.

sections.label: Flexible work over mandatory leave
sections.summary: It states feedback from NTUC is that mandatory leave of a few days may be insufficient, and flexible work arrangements are more sustainable for daily elderly care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We have been working closely with the Singapore National Employers Federation, as well as with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC).

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And the feedback that we get, especially from NTUC, the workers, is that the mandatory leave is, if it is just a few days, it may not be sufficient, because if you are taking care of an elderly parent, it is actually a daily need; it is not just one or two days per year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Instead, building flexibility into work arrangements, whether it is part-time work, staggered working hours or even hybrid work, working from home on some days every week, these are better appreciated and more sustainable for employees who have to take care of their elderly family members, on a prolonged period, every day.
